solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bovine creature following small island bird

parts.note: a male of the cattle family
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in a page reference
an inch is a small island in Scottish usage

explanation.surface: A cow seems to trail behind a little island, as if wading across to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is the abbreviation f.; INCH as an islet is common in Scottish place names such as Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfinch is a stout European songbird with a rosy breast in the male.

clue.text: Foundations of army garrisons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the supports things rest on
second meaning: military stations where troops are quartered

explanation.surface: Someone is inspecting how military garrisons were originally laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers both the bottom supports of structures and the military camps from which forces operate.

clue.text: Shelter, having a smoke in greenery

indicators.note: to have something in is to hold it inside, so one word is wrapped around the other
completes 'having ... in', placing the smoke inside the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone takes a cigarette break, sheltering among the leaves of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage collectively, the green leaves of plants, so it is a synonym of greenery.

clue.text: Display bill: it's a critical moment

parts.note: to flash something is to show it off briefly
a bill is a narrow headland, as in Portland Bill, and so is a point

explanation.surface: Putting up a poster turns out to be the moment a dispute erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests a poster or invoice; here it is a promontory, like Portland Bill on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashpoint is the moment or place at which tension breaks out into violence or crisis.

clue.text: Out climbing, finds radioactive element?

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: out means not in, two words run together

explanation.surface: A climber who is out on the mountain stumbles upon something radioactive.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the dated name: niton was an early name for radon.
explanation.definitionFit: Niton was the name given to radon, the radioactive noble gas, early in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Prominent performer owned vessel touring East

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the outer letters surround the compass point

parts.note: had means possessed
a liner is a large passenger ship
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A star singer owns a cruise ship sailing round the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owned vessel' reads like a ship someone possesses; the past tense of own is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the star act whose name is billed most prominently on a show.

clue.text: Rock a prince found in the Kent area

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Kent lies in South East England, abbreviated SE
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A royal is discovered hiding among the rocks of the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is a fine-grained sedimentary rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: Behaved disgustingly in petty quarrel!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: expelled saliva, a rude act

explanation.surface: Someone behaved badly during a trivial row.
explanation.definitionFit: As a past-tense verb it describes ejecting saliva; as a noun it names a short trivial argument.

clue.text: I'm welcomed by a security organisation, being notedly lively

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so the first words go within the organisation

parts.note: taken as written
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a defence alliance
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerfully received by a defence alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' means in musical notation, signalling an Italian tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Animato is an Italian direction on a score telling the player to perform in a spirited, animated way.

clue.text: Old coach having left area, thus lying outside

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so the letter for area drops out of the coach word

parts.note: to coach is to train
A is the abbreviation for area
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A former trainer who has quit the region is now an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus but is the verb train.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means coming from or situated outside, the opposite of intrinsic.

clue.text: Man investing in firm substance for stopping leaks

indicators.note: to invest in a firm is to put something into it, so the name goes inside

parts.note: set means firm or hardened
a man's name

explanation.surface: A businessman puts money into a company that makes waterproofing products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective set, as in a set jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is any material applied to close gaps and keep water or air out.

clue.text: A disheartened spiritual leader initially serving this scholar

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A depressed religious leader is first to help a learned academic.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBI has five letters, so its heart is the middle B.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar who specialises in Arabic language or Arab culture.

clue.text: Giddy gals in yacht abandoning area scornfully

indicators.note: someone giddy is dizzy and reeling, so the letters spin into a new order
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the letters taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Dizzy girls on a yacht leave the scene, sneering as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one A of the two in the phrase is removed before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak scathingly is to speak with harsh, withering contempt, which is scornful.

clue.text: African country's evil intent ignored by Anglican church

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the church letters drop away

parts.note: malice is the wish to do harm
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church overlooks a nation's ill will.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked state in West Africa whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Grating, one obstructing harbour clearances

parts.note: a port is a harbour

indicators.note: something obstructing a passage sits in the middle of it, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: culls are selective removals or killings
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something is blocking the clearing of the dock area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like an adjective meaning irritating; it is the noun, a lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy iron or wooden lattice gate lowered to bar a castle gateway.

clue.text: Communist, commander without a set of beliefs

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
red is the traditional label for a communist

explanation.surface: A communist officer is said to have no convictions at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking; it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, the statement of principles or faith a person or group holds.

clue.text: Endless opportunity to keep horse and coach

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the horse goes inside
something endless has lost its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: An unlimited opportunity to own a horse and carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' here is a motor coach, not a trainer or a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an early open motor coach, used for outings in Britain.

clue.text: Showing bitterness, managed business right round America

parts.note: ran means ran a business, managed
Co. is the abbreviation for company
R is the abbreviation for right
the letter O is round in shape
the United States

explanation.surface: An embittered executive ran a company right across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container signal; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of rancour, a deep lingering resentment.

clue.text: Turned up about gold missing from bottom drawer?

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: what is missing from something has been taken out of it, so those letters go

parts.note: a bottom drawer is the British name for a bride's store of linen, a trousseau
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone finds the gold gone from the lowest drawer of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bottom drawer is the linen and household goods a woman collected before marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose whose tip is turned upwards.

clue.text: Patterned carpet unknown in a big church

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the church phrase

parts.note: a minster is a large church, like York Minster
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: There is a mystery hidden in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: X slips in after the A, before MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of machine-woven pile carpet named after the Devon town.

clue.text: Weakling takes full advantage of surgical procedure

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it fully
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A feeble patient makes the most of their operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a timid, ineffectual person lacking courage.

clue.text: Subject to film?

parts.note: taken as written
pic is informal for a picture, a film

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a question about something being liable to filming; 'Subject' is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject or theme of a discussion or piece of writing.

clue.text: Indian given injection in quiet place of learning

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: in places the jab inside the quiet place of learning

parts.note: uni is short for university
a jab is an injection

explanation.surface: A man from India gets a vaccination at a quiet college.
explanation.walkthrough: In musical notation p, for piano, means quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Punjabi is a person from the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Colleague removing last of garbage from narrow street

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so that letter comes out

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A workmate clears rubbish out of a back lane.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate who works alongside one, broadly a colleague.

clue.text: Way athlete identifies crested bird

parts.note: a road is a way
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: A sprinter on the road spots a bird by its crest.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a crested ground cuckoo of the American south-west that runs fast.

clue.text: Party in lead is Conservative

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: The Tories are leading in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party, encouraged by 'Conservative'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club night where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Fairly short, though blooming early once!

indicators.note: a short word has been cut, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: rather means fairly, somewhat

explanation.surface: Something rather brief nevertheless flowers early.
explanation.walkthrough: Once signals an archaic word: Milton wrote of the rathe primrose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic adjective for early, used especially of flowers and fruit appearing early in the season.

clue.text: Ruler accommodating Zulu in estate, perhaps

indicators.note: to accommodate someone is to give them room inside, so a letter goes in

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, a station wagon
Zulu is the radio alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A monarch shelters a Zulu on his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests land; in Britain an estate is also a car with a large boot, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A czar or tsar was the emperor of Russia, an absolute ruler.

clue.text: A measure is announced for old court sessions

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a size is a measure

explanation.surface: A new rule is declared affecting the historic law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic sittings of judges in English counties, abolished in 1971.

clue.text: Jumping insect pursuing old sailor

indicators.note: what pursues comes behind, so the insect goes after the sailor

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A leaping bug chases an elderly seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltant is a heraldic and technical term for leaping or dancing, from Latin saltare.

clue.text: One who gets by as a horse dealer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who manages in difficulty
second meaning: an old word for a trader in horses

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes a living trading horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is someone who copes, and also, from an old verb to cope meaning barter, a horse trader.

clue.text: Going round Greek island one sees a lively dance

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the rearranged letters wrap the island
lively suggests jumping about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I; the rest taken as written
Cos, or Kos, is a Dodecanese island

explanation.surface: A tourist touring a Greek island watches some energetic dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lively dance' reads as one phrase; 'lively' is the anagram signal and 'dance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The écossaise is a quick country dance in duple time, its name French for Scottish.
